chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a garment that is dyed with saffron, then washed; can I wear it while I am in Ihram? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. Saffron is not from the perfumes, but I dislike that you wear what makes you prominent among the people.

key_terms.الطِّيب: Perfume/scent (specifically the scent of plants, forbidden for the muhrim)
key_terms.الْعُصْفُر: Saffron, a yellow dye and spice
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear saffron-dyed clothes during Hajj Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that saffron-dyed garments are permissible in Ihram because saffron is classified as a colorant rather than a perfume (tayyib), distinguishing it from items prohibited due to scent. However, he introduces a layer of practical jurisprudence by expressing dislike (karahah) if the distinctive scent causes the wearer to be singled out or recognized by others, highlighting the balance between ritual validity and social modesty. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on both the literal definition of prohibited items and the contextual impact of Ihram attire on the pilgrim's state of humility.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Hilal who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the clothes which happen to be dyed with saffron, then it is washed, ‘Can I wear it and I am in Ihraam?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes. The saffron is not from the perfumes, but Iasws dislike it if you were to wear what makes you to be prominent among the people’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the cloth which is stained with saffron and it then is washed but it (the stain) does not go away; if it can be used for Ihram.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if its smell is gone; even if all of it is colored which has become of a whitish color, when washed; then it is not harmful.’”
